blocks.text: Keep these two words together as one memorised greeting. This is the formal model, usable at any time of day. Use it for a boss or cashier rather than the informal peer greeting. A teacher is also a formal addressee. Listen again, repeat the complete greeting, and give that greeting back aloud without analysing its words.

This printed greeting appears in a list of polite words. It is a spelling model, rather than a teacher's spoken turn. Recall the formal greeting you heard while looking at this printed model; this is not a letter-reading task.

Two peers meet at the classroom entrance. Their exchange uses the informal greeting. Compare their greeting with the printed model already shown. For a teacher, receptionist or cashier, choose the separate formal model. The social situation guides your choice; the printed quotation supplies spelling, not the register rule. First identify who is being greeted. Then recognise the matching chunk in the model. Keep the peers' dialogue informal when practising their turns.

lessons.title: привіт
lessons.job: Hear an informal or formal first greeting and say the appropriate memorised response aloud.
lessons.rationale: D3 chunks come first by ear as in ULP S1 lessons 1–2; do not decode their unseen letters or analyse adjective, noun, or case forms. A 210-word target gives two short Ukrainian-first models, English context support, and explicit out-loud practice without padding.

steps.teach: Play only the informal V-001 peer greeting; show the Ukrainian model beside English support, then repeat and respond aloud as a whole D3 chunk on X-001. Do not decode names or letters. T-002 grounds the peer register through explains only; premium notes are never quoted.

Introduce and play the formal V-002 greeting as the intact W-075+W-076 chunk, then contrast it with W-074 by social situation before a4. T-002 grounds boss/cashier boundaries; T-020 grounds the receptionist. T-021 establishes only that a teacher is a formal addressee, not a greeting quotation. Repeat and give the matching spoken response on X-001. ULP records remain explains-only; premium notes are never quoted.

Display the attributed public T-040 printed spelling of Добрий день once, paired with English. It is a list of polite words, not a teacher speaking. T-041 explains formal register; T-021 identifies a teacher as a formal addressee. Premium notes are grounding only.

After both recorded greeting introductions and the single T-040 display in s3, present the informal peer dialogue with paired English. Compare that dialogue with the already displayed printed spelling of Добрий день; do not repeat the quote. English establishes the friend versus teacher, receptionist or cashier situation from T-002/T-020/T-021. T-041 explains formal register; the public quote supplies only spelling. Both hosts precede a2/a4/a5; no greeting or name spelling is a decoding target.
